findings.message:
https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/d6bbfd1e10a3078e37db546f7d0b76bfdc2f419b/library/core/src/fmt/num.rs#L621

smaller types are delegated to u32/u64 on 32/64bit, so this will assert u32/u64 buffer size for e.g. u8, so

```rs
    let mut buf = NumBuffer::<u8>::new();
    let s = 7u8.format_into(&mut buf);
```

panics here. Not sure if there is a way that works without just making this function `unsafe` and moving the safety assertion to the call in the _small function below?

*[View changes since the review](https://triagebot.infra.rust-lang.org/gh-changes-since/rust-lang/rust/165284/349bba62f1838cbd9b453ffda272c6972754122d..d6bbfd1e10a3078e37db546f7d0b76bfdc2f419b)*
findings.tp_fp_justification: seritools: the assert uses $T::MAX.ilog10 for the buffer bound, but u8/u16 delegate to the larger-type implementation, so e.g. 7u8.format_into() always panics.
